title: gf2-core SpBitMatrix sparse-dense matmat for GF(2)
description:
Add a public `SpBitMatrix::matmat(&self, b: &BitMatrix) -> BitMatrix` method (sparse × dense → dense over GF(2)) and wire it into `bench_sparse_csv_emitter.rs` as a `sparse×dense,GF(2)` row. Closes the `sparse×dense × GF(2)` cell currently marked `not-yet-harnessed` on both sides per 47698404 scorecard § 5 #6.

## Background

47698404 surfaced that `SpBitMatrix` exposes no sparse×dense entry-point — only `SpBitMatrix::matmul` (sparse × sparse). The closest path is round-trip through `to_dense()` and `BitMatrix::gemm`, which is dense×dense and not the same algorithm. The design doc (`dev/plans/sparse_benchmark_corpus.md:168`) names this cell as a hard reference cell with LinBox `applyLeft` as canonical reference.

This task implements the gf2-core side; the LinBox-side reference harness extension is a sibling follow-up.

## Naming convention note (lead-clarification, 2026-05-05)

The CSV operation key is `sparse×dense` (Unicode multiplication sign U+00D7), matching the project-wide convention formalised in `dev/plans/sota_reference_acceptance_protocol.md` § 7 CSV schema and `benchmarks/analyze.py`. The original session-5 issue text used `sparse_dense` (underscore); that was a typo on the part of the lead's autonomous filing — the convention is the Unicode form.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] `SpBitMatrix::matmat(&self, b: &BitMatrix) -> BitMatrix` lands in `crates/gf2-core/src/sparse.rs` with doctests.
- [hard] Tests cover word-boundary cases (n ∈ {0, 1, 63, 64, 65, 1023, 1024, 1025}) and verify equality vs `self.to_dense().matmul(b)`.
- [hard] Property test (proptest) over random sparse + random dense matrices verifies bitwise equality with the round-trip-dense path on n ∈ [1, 256].
- [hard] `bench_sparse_csv_emitter.rs --quick` emits a `sparse×dense,GF(2)` row at n=1024.
- [hard] Smoke at n=16 in `benchmarks/reference/sparse_smoke.cpp` cross-checks the new `SpBitMatrix::matmat` output. Baseline: an in-harness scalar reference (`scalar_sparse_dense` in sparse_smoke.cpp); upgrade to direct gf2-core integration is tracked by 96fde7c7 (the verification-work follow-up that establishes the gf2-core-from-C++ ground-truth-file mechanism). Until 96fde7c7 lands, the scalar-reference branch is the active deliverable per protocol § 9 Amendment 2 (`not-yet-harnessed`/`no-independent-oracle` markers).
- [hard] `cargo-ci`, `code-review`, `doc-review` pass.
